name_zh: 图尔博茶园大吉岭红茶
processing: Darjeeling tea, with orthodox making typical of the district and oxidation set by the flush.
harvest_season: Not recorded in detail for this garden. Spring and summer flushes are the best-known Darjeeling pickings.
appearance_dry: Typically twisted olive-brown leaf with some pale tips.
appearance_liquor: Bright gold to amber, depending on the flush.
taste_profile: Thurbo teas are known for an unusual fragrance. Typical of Darjeeling, spring lots lean floral and summer lots add fruit and body.

brewing.notes: Western-style. Keep the water a little off the boil to protect the aroma this garden is valued for.

vintage_note: Sold by year and flush, and it can command premium prices. Spring lots of the current year are worth seeking fresh; summer lots keep a little better.
description:
Thurbo is a Mirik garden owned by the Goodricke Group, which also holds Castleton, Margaret's Hope, Badamtam and Barnesbeg. It spans a very wide height range, from about 980 to 2,440 metres, with the Mechi to the north and the Rangbag to the south.

The climate is typical of the hills, with cool temperatures and limited sun, and the garden is valued for fragrance. How it handles each flush is not closely documented, though orthodox making is the district's norm.

Expect aroma first. As with other Darjeelings, a spring lot is light and floral, a summer one rounder. Slightly cooler water helps keep the fragrance from being overrun.

Its teas can carry premium prices, so a stated year and flush are the minimum you should ask for. If you enjoy it, trying a Castleton or Margaret's Hope from the same group makes an easy comparison.
history:
The name is said to be a variant of the Nepali word for tent, from British tents pitched here during fighting with the Nepalese, a story dated to 1870; the date looks doubtful for such fighting and is best taken as local tradition. The garden was planted in 1872.

In 1969 the West Bengal tourism department began acquiring 335 acres of the estate, land that was developed into the Mirik lake area.
